Traditional Christmas Roast

Served at: St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day)

Serves 6-8Prep 20 minCook 1 hr 30 min

A Christmas Roast is a classic centerpiece for St. Stephen's Day, also known as Boxing Day, celebrated on December 26th. This hearty roast brings family and friends together to enjoy the festive spirit with rich flavors and comforting sides, often using leftover ingredients from Christmas Day or freshly prepared meats.

Ingredients

  • 4-5 lb (1.8-2.3 kg) beef rib roast or turkey breast
  • 2 tbsp (30 ml) olive oil
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh rosemary, chopped
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) fresh thyme, chopped
  • 1 tsp (5 ml) salt
  • 1 tsp (5 ml) black pepper
  • 1 cup (240 ml) beef or chicken broth
  • 2 large onions, quartered
  • 4 carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
  • 4 parsnips, peeled and cut into chunks
  • 2 tbsp (30 g) butter

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a small bowl, mix olive oil, minced garlic, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.
  3. Rub the mixture all over the roast evenly.
  4. Place the roast on a rack in a roasting pan and surround it with onions, carrots, and parsnips.
  5. Pour broth into the bottom of the pan to keep the meat moist.
  6. Roast in the oven for about 1 hour and 30 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 135°F (57°C) for medium-rare beef, or 165°F (74°C) for turkey.
  7. Baste the roast occasionally with pan juices to keep it flavorful and moist.
  8. Remove the roast from the oven and let it rest for 15 minutes before carving.
  9. While the roast rests, melt butter in a pan and sauté the roasted vegetables briefly to enhance flavor.
  10. Carve the roast and serve with the roasted vegetables and pan juices.

Tips

  • Use a meat thermometer to ensure perfect doneness.
  • For a more festive touch, add cranberries or chestnuts to the roasting pan.
  • Leftover roast can be used in sandwiches or stews the following day.
